claims.sourceText: CRS Report R44629, 'Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs): Background and Issues for Congress'
claims.text: FAR 35.017 grants FFRDCs access to government and supplier data, including sensitive and proprietary information, and to employees and facilities beyond that common in a normal contractual relationship.
As of February 2026, 41 FFRDCs were sponsored or co-sponsored by 12 federal agencies.

FFRDCs must operate in the public interest with objectivity and independence, be free from organisational conflicts of interest, fully disclose their activities to their sponsoring agency, and may not use their special access to compete with the private sector for federal R&D contracts.

edges.label: FAR 35.017 is the regulation that creates the seam
edges.note: The subpart grants FFRDCs access to government and supplier data beyond a normal contractual relationship while requiring disclosure only to the sponsoring agency.

edges.label: the FFRDC seam is a species of contracting mechanics, not a separate subject
edges.note: FAR 35.017 is a procurement regulation. The records status, disclosure direction and sole-source features that make the FFRDC form load-bearing on this board are all properties of the contracting instrument, which is why the seam domain should hang off contracting mechanics rather than float beside it.

edges.label: the largest operator of the one acquisition form built to be non-competitive by design
edges.note: MITRE operates multiple FFRDCs. FAR 35.017 permits an agency to meet special long-term research needs through a sponsoring agreement with a single operator outside full and open competition, and obliges the FFRDC to disclose its activities to its sponsor and to no one else. That is a contracting mechanism, and MITRE is its largest single instance.
